title: Software for Startups: Build a Maintainable Tech Stack
description: A practical startup software guide covering customer management, project work, communication, development, analytics and payments. Recommendations are evaluation starting points, not verified rankings; confirm current plans, limits and startup terms with vendors.
challenges: Limited time and budget make it important to prioritize tools that remove a real bottleneck rather than buying overlapping subscriptions.
Early workflows change quickly, so the stack should support exports, clear ownership and a manageable path to migration.
Small teams need collaboration and documentation without creating excessive notifications, duplicated status updates or administrative overhead.
Product and marketing decisions need trustworthy measurement, but analytics only helps when events, definitions and data quality are maintained.
Customer and employee data require least-privilege access, secure secrets, backups and a clear owner even before the company has a dedicated security team.

recommendations.bestFor: Evaluate for contact and deal tracking if the startup needs a structured sales pipeline. Verify current free or paid plan limits, user roles, automation, export and whether required marketing or service workflows need separate products.

Evaluate for software teams that want issue tracking, triage and cycle-based planning. Test the team's real workflow, reporting, integrations and permissions; confirm the current plan supports the required seats and controls.

Evaluate for channel-based coordination and integrations when the team has a clear communication policy. Test search, guest access, notifications, retention and how important decisions are captured outside chat.

Evaluate for source control, code review and CI workflows. Test branch protections, required checks, secret handling, release permissions and recovery; confirm build minutes and other limits directly.
Evaluate for event-based product questions such as onboarding funnels or retention. Define an event taxonomy, validate data quality and verify current event, retention, export and seat limits.

Evaluate for payment acceptance or subscription workflows that match the business model and supported countries. Confirm fees, payout timing, dispute handling, tax responsibilities and integration scope in current official terms.

rows: HubSpot — consider for contact records, deal stages and customer handoffs.
Current plan limits, user roles, automation, export and product boundaries.
Linear — consider for engineering issue tracking and planning.
Workflow fit, reporting, integrations, permissions and administration.
Slack — consider for team messaging and tool notifications.
Search, guest access, retention, notification policy and decision records.
GitHub — consider for repositories, reviews and CI checks.
Branch protection, secrets, build limits, deployment and rollback.
Mixpanel — consider for event-based product analysis.
Event taxonomy, identity rules, privacy, retention and export.
Stripe — consider for payment acceptance or subscription billing.
Regional availability, fees, payouts, disputes, taxes and reconciliation.

faqs.question: Should a startup use one all-in-one suite?
faqs.answer: Only if the suite supports the required workflows without forcing costly workarounds. Map systems of record, test integrations and compare the administration burden with a smaller set of specialist tools.

faqs.question: How should a startup prioritize tools?
faqs.answer: Prioritize by business risk and repeated friction: customer records, delivery workflow, access security, backups and measurement. Defer tools that do not solve a defined problem.

faqs.question: Are the recommendations ranked by verified ratings?
faqs.answer: No. They are starting points for evaluation, not independently verified rankings. Run a pilot and confirm current product and plan details with each vendor.

faqs.question: How can a startup keep costs under control?
faqs.answer: Track seats, usage, add-ons, renewal dates and duplicate capabilities. Assign an owner to each subscription and include migration, training and internal administration in the cost.

faqs.question: What should be checked before adopting a tool?
faqs.answer: Test the main workflow, permissions, export, integrations, backups and offboarding. Confirm current plan limits and data-handling terms in writing.
